column1: # Book 3 second-round read (Fable, 2026-10-30): every line read against the Latin. No changes.
# 3.614 ire foras ... relinquere still depends on conquereretur: the mind would lament its going out, not go out.

column2: but rather that it went out and left its garment, like a snake.

column1: # 3.657-658 the three ablative absolutes (tongue flickering, tail threatening, body long) had been run together so that the tongue threatened.

column2: What is more, if, its tongue flickering, its tail threatening,
a serpent's, with its long body, both of them
